question: Turn one thing on or off

candidates.pick: The change takes effect immediately, with no Save button
The change is saved together with a form
The state belongs to the current item and sits in a toolbar, such as mute or favorite

question: Choose one of a few options

candidates.pick: There are two to about five options inside a form and each should be read before choosing
There are two to five short options and the choice applies at once, such as a view or unit
Space is too tight to show the options and a default suits most people

question: Choose one of many options

candidates.pick: There are roughly 5 to 15 familiar options
There are more than about 15 options, or users know the name of what they want
Every option must be visible and compared, and there is room for all of them

question: Choose several options

candidates.pick: There are up to about ten options and all can be shown
The list is long or users can add their own values
Only one value is needed after all, from a long list

question: Enter a date

candidates.pick: The user knows the date by heart or reads it from a document, such as a date of birth
The date is chosen in relation to today, a weekday or availability, or it is a range
Only a handful of dates are possible, such as delivery slots

question: Enter a number

candidates.pick: The value is exact, large or not a quantity, such as an amount or a reference number

An approximate value in a bounded range is enough and its effect is visible while dragging
